title: U.S. House · Virginia's 5th District
area: Virginia's 5th Congressional District (Southside and Central Virginia, including Lynchburg, Danville, and Charlottesville-area exurbs)

context.text: Incumbent John McGuire defeated Melanie Lucero in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary, 84.4% to 15.6%. Former Rep. Bob Good, whom McGuire defeated in the 2024 Republican primary, did not qualify for the 2026 primary ballot. Tom Perriello, who represented this district in Congress from 2009 to 2011, won the Democratic primary with 79.8% of the vote over Suzanne Krzyzanowski and Robert Tracinski.

summary.text: John McGuire is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Virginia's 5th District, elected in 2024 after defeating then-incumbent Bob Good in the Republican primary. He is a former Navy SEAL who previously served in the Virginia House of Delegates and briefly in the Virginia Senate.

background.text: Born in Richmond, Virginia in 1968; graduated from Henrico High School; served as a U.S. Navy SEAL from 1988 to 1998.
Founded SEAL Team Physical Training Inc. after his military service.
Served in the Virginia House of Delegates (District 56, 2018-2024) and briefly in the Virginia State Senate (District 10, 2024) before his election to Congress in 2024.

positions.summary: In a March 2026 press release he said he voted against a War Powers Resolution and that President Trump's military actions against Iran are within the President's authority under Article II.
positions.quote: As Commander-in-Chief, President Trump's actions against Iran are well within his authority under Article II of the Constitution.

positions.summary: In a February 2026 press release he backed the SAVE America Act's requirement of documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote and urged the Senate to pass it.
positions.quote: By requiring photo ID to vote and proof of citizenship to register, we are taking real measures

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Subcommittees on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation; Health Care and Financial Services; and Military and Foreign Affairs) and the House Committee on Armed Services in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Tom Perriello
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 79.8% of the vote

summary.text: Tom Perriello previously represented Virginia's 5th District in Congress from 2009 to 2011. He is a Yale-trained attorney whose career since leaving Congress has included international human-rights and diplomatic work and leadership at the Center for American Progress Action Fund.

background.text: Earned a J.D. from Yale Law School in 2001; worked as an advisor to the international prosecutor of the Special Court for Sierra Leone and on international justice efforts in Kosovo, Darfur, and Afghanistan.
Represented Virginia's 5th District in the U.S. House from 2009 to 2011, serving on the House Committees on Veterans' Affairs and on Transportation and Infrastructure; lost re-election in 2010.

Served as CEO of the Center for American Progress Action Fund, directed the State Department's 2014 Quadrennial Diplomacy and Development Review, and was appointed by President Obama in 2015 as special envoy for the Great Lakes Region of Africa.

positions.summary: His campaign issues page lists ending the current tariffs as his most urgent priority, citing their effect on grocery prices.
positions.quote: Tom's most urgent priority will be to save families money by ending the tariffs that spiked grocery bills

positions.summary: His campaign foreign-policy page says Congress should restore its role in authorizing foreign wars and states a rule that Congress vote before the U.S. fights.
positions.quote: Tom's rule is simple: Make Congress vote before America fights, and fund the people who stop wars before they start.

positions.summary: His campaign housing page calls for building more housing and cutting red tape to bring costs down.
positions.quote: That means building more housing, cutting red tape, and taking on the corporate practices that are driving prices higher.

record.text: As a member of Congress (2009-2011), voted for the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act and the Affordable Care Act, according to his own campaign account of his record.

summary.text: Cooke Harvey is an independent candidate running in Virginia's 5th Congressional District general election.
